source_text: Natura - inquis - humana, si malum esset, salvanda non esset; si ei mali nihil inesset, salvanda non esset [n249] . Quid aliud ostendisti quam unam rem propter id debere salvari, propter quod illam negaveras debere salvari?
pass_a_gloss: Nature, you say, human, if it were evil, would not be to be saved; if nothing of evil were in it, it would not be to be saved. What else have you shown than that one thing ought to be saved on account of that on account of which you had denied it ought to be saved?

lemmas.lexica: LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: ‘If human nature were evil,’ you say, ‘it ought not to be saved; if no evil were within it, it would not need to be saved’ (Augustine, Marriage and Sexual Desire 2.36). What have you shown except that one thing ought to be saved for the very reason you had denied that it ought to be saved?

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
